synopsis: ISO 3450:2011, reconfirmed in September 2022, specifies service, secondary and parking-brake performance and tests for wheeled and high-speed rubber-tracked earth-moving machines; ISO 10265:2008 covers crawlers at 20 km/h or less [f10651, f15190, f5979]. ISO 3450 measures stopping distance from brake-control actuation to standstill, including brake-system response but excluding operator reaction, and requires the most adverse braking configuration, including maximum specified payload for dumpers and certain other machines [f5976, f5967, f5968]. Stopping distance is not the sole acceptance outcome because controllability also matters, and passing ISO 3450 does not establish that perception, classification, threat assessment or trigger logic work [f6149, f2361]. The proposed four-month validation plan uses ISO 21815-3 CxS distances calculated for each machine model from ISO 3450 brake data and declared delays; physical brake testing remains necessary, with no identified off-road document accepting simulation as a replacement for prescribed physical tests [f2638, f10431, f2103]. These standards do not establish a calibration-stop count that guarantees prediction across 100-plus site types, multiple brake architectures and all stated weather conditions, supporting separate machine-family braking models rather than assuming universal transfer [f6162, f6163, f13733]. Verification is uneven across chapters: some report scope and edition details, while others say ISO 10265 or ISO 3450 details were not verified; the reported 32 km/h or 80%-of-maximum test speed and stopping-distance formulas come from secondary material requiring confirmation against the standard [f8946, f8947, f2197, f7013, f11197, f15193, f2436].
